Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[-1,2]\times [-2,1]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)=2x{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}y+3{x}^{2}.
$$

Calculate the second iteration of the Newton-Raphson process for optimization that starts at ${x}_{0}=[2,\,-2]^{T}$ if the first iteration of the algorithm gives ${x}_{1}=[1.75,\,0.125]^{T}.$ Round your final answer to three decimal places (if needed).

Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[0,1]\times [0,1]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)=4{x}^{2}y-3x{y}^{2}+{x}^{2}-2x.
$$

Fill in the blanks in the matrix equation below that defines the first iteration of the Newton-Raphson process starting at the point $[1,\,1]^{T},$ and compute the components of the first iteration. Round the answer for ${x}_{1}$ to **three decimal places**.

| $[$ | {{field-1}} | $2$ | $]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})\,=[$ | $-5$ | $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $2$ | {{field-2}} | {{field-3}} |  |  |  |

| ${x}_{1}≈[$ | $0.594$ | $]$ |

feedback.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{H}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}∇f({x}_{n}),
$$

where $H({x}_{n})$ and $∇f({x}_{n})$ are the Hessian and gradient of $f$, respectively, evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

Equivalently, at each iteration, the above equation can be rewritten as

$$
{H}_{f}({x}_{n})({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-∇f({x}_{n}).
$$

In our case, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(4{x}^{2}y-3x{y}^{2}+{x}^{2}-2x) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(4{x}^{2}y-3x{y}^{2}+{x}^{2}-2x)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8xy-3{y}^{2}+2x-2 \\ 4{x}^{2}-6xy\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

and the Hessian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(8xy-3{y}^{2}+2x-2) & \frac{∂}{∂x}(4{x}^{2}-6xy) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(8xy-3{y}^{2}+2x-2) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(4{x}^{2}-6xy)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8y+2 & 8x-6y \\ 8x-6y & -6x\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson system of equations is

$$
{[\begin{aligned}8y+2 & 8x-6y \\ 8x-6y & -6x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-{[\begin{aligned}8xy-3{y}^{2}+2x-2 \\ 4{x}^{2}-6xy\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\begin{aligned}8y+2 & 8x-6y \\ 8x-6y & -6x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-{[\begin{aligned}8xy-3{y}^{2}+2x-2 \\ 4{x}^{2}-6xy\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\ [\begin{aligned}8(1)+2 & 8(1)-6(1) \\ 8(1)-6(1) & -6(1)\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-[\begin{aligned}8(1)(1)-3(1)^{2}+2(1)-2 \\ 4(1)^{2}-6(1)(1)\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}10 & 2 \\ 2 & -6\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system of equations, we get $({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})=[\begin{aligned}-13/32 \\ -15/32\end{aligned}].$ Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}+[\begin{aligned}-\frac{13}{32} \\ -\frac{15}{32}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-\frac{13}{32} \\ -\frac{15}{32}\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}0.594 \\ 0.531\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
